overview: Neville's July 1930 report explains Japan chose Anshan over Sinuiju for the Showa Steel Works after the South Manchuria Railway president discussed it with the Overseas Affairs Minister; subsidies and tariffs favored Anshan, with the railway-affiliated firm capitalized at ¥100 million for 500,000-ton capacity.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomat in Japan and sender identified by the filing sheet

people.name: Mitsugi Sengoku
people.role: President of the South Manchuria Railway Company

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Neville report on the Showa Steel Works
subfiles.about: The sheet directs readers to another decimal-file location and summarizes the decision to establish the Showa Steel Works at Anshan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Neville's 1930 report: Anshan was virtually chosen over Sinuiju for the Showa Steel Works, capitalized at ¥100 million.

subfiles.title: Report extract on selection of Anshan for the Showa Steel Works
subfiles.about: The enclosure reports the near-final selection of Anshan over Sinuiju as the site of the proposed Showa Steel Works.
subfiles.summary: Report says Anshan was effectively chosen for the Showa Steel Works after Sengoku discussed it with Japan's Overseas Affairs Minister, aided by subsidies and tariffs, with the railway-affiliated firm capitalized at ¥100 million for 500,000-ton capacity.

interest: Shows Japan's 1930 decision to site the Showa Steel Works at Anshan over Sinuiju, favored by subsidies and tariffs.
